programme: SIN3A anchors a SIN3A/HDAC corepressor scaffold; together with the BET-bromodomain reader BRD4 and the HIPK2–HDAC3 axis, this sets the chromatin state at inflammatory/oxidative-stress loci in blood leukocytes. MAFG (the small-Maf partner of the Nrf2/NFE2L pathway) drives the antioxidant-response targets NQO1, HMOX1 and NFE2L1 at such loci, while STAT6 supplies cytokine-driven (IL4/IL13, M2/microglial-polarization) transcriptional input that this chromatin machinery gates.
role_in_a: Not directly evidenced in the retrieved record (no Open Targets hit and no paper places any of these factors in fibromyalgia). If this programme is relevant, it would be as the chromatin/oxidative-stress control layer underlying the low-grade peripheral immune activation and oxidative stress repeatedly proposed in fibromyalgia pathophysiology — but that link is not documented here.
role_in_b: Documented in the retrieved record: BRD4 chromatin reading controls blood-brain-barrier integrity and hemin/ferroptosis-driven neuroinflammation after ischemia (PMID 41267382, 40605044); the HIPK2–HDAC3 axis drives neuronal mitochondrial fragmentation in stroke injury (PMID 39079624); STAT6 directs microglial M2 polarization and senescence programs in cerebral small-vessel disease, acute ischemia and central post-stroke pain (PMID 42467351, 42070316, 40675266, 40848997). SIN3A and MAFG sit at percentile 0.90/absent in Open Targets stroke scoring but have no disease-specific paper support.
shared_axis: If the same SIN3A/BRD4/HIPK2 chromatin-corepressor machinery gates MAFG-driven oxidative-stress genes and STAT6-driven cytokine/polarization genes in circulating leukocytes generally, both a chronic peripheral oxidative/immune state (fibromyalgia) and an acute cerebrovascular oxidative-inflammatory insult (stroke) would recruit the same blood-cell transcriptional control layer, differing in intensity and duration of trigger rather than in the machinery used.
reasoning: The module is nameable — SIN3A/BRD4/HIPK2 as chromatin corepressor/reader machinery, MAFG for oxidative-stress output, STAT6 for cytokine/polarization input — and stroke's involvement is independently documented for three of the five carrying factors. But no retrieved article connects fibromyalgia to this programme; the fibromyalgia side rests on the general oxidative-stress/immune hypothesis for that disease, not on anything retrieved, so the pairing counts as unexpected rather than supported. Strength is moderate, not strong, because SIN3A (the most concordant factor, 12/12) and MAFG have zero disease-specific literature placement despite carrying the model mechanistically.
support: PMID 41267382 — BRD4 BD1 antagonism preserves blood-brain barrier integrity via Rnf43/β-catenin signaling in a stroke model. PMID 40605044 — BRD4 silencing attenuates hemin-induced neuronal ferroptosis and inflammation via H3K27ac-ATF3 in cerebral injury. PMID 39079624 — neuronal HIPK2-HDAC3 axis regulates mitochondrial fragmentation in stroke injury. PMID 42467351 — STAT6 regulates microglial senescence/autophagy in cognitive impairment after cerebral small vessel disease. PMID 42070316 — electroacupuncture modulates STAT6/PPARγ binding to promote M2 microglial polarization post-stroke. PMID 40848997 — LXR-β regulates microglial efferocytosis and neuroinflammation via STAT6 activation in central post-stroke pain.
how_to_falsify: Profile PBMCs/whole blood from fibromyalgia patients versus matched controls for SIN3A/BRD4 chromatin occupancy (ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN) at MAFG target promoters (NQO1, HMOX1, NFE2L1) and at STAT6 target genes, alongside HIPK2-HDAC3 activity readouts; if fibromyalgia leukocytes show no enrichment or activation of this chromatin/oxidative-stress signature relative to controls, the proposed shared axis is wrong, since the account predicts this specific module — not generic inflammation — should be engaged in both conditions.
caveats: Both cohorts are blood/blood, so the tissue pairing is trivial and does not itself support cross-disease relevance. Only 12 patient-group comparisons were available, drawn from just 2 independent cohort pairs — thin grounds for generalizing, especially for factors at 7-8/12 concordance (KLF3, HIPK2, MAFG, LHX9, GRHL3, DMTF1, STAT6, RFX2, ZNF236). Nine single-view factors (TOX2, KDM5C, POU6F2, TCF21, PIN1, RXRG, FOXD3, ZNF571, NSD2) were excluded because they each topped only one subgroup — none are used here. STAT1, along with JUNB/SMAD3/STAT5A/CEBPD/ETS2/BCL3/NR3C2/IRF8/LITAF/FOS/E2F3, was removed as tissue-generic; that excludes the canonical ISGF3/interferon partner of STAT2/IRF9-type stories, so no interferon-signature account should be built around STAT6 alone. Fibromyalgia has no Open Targets association and no retrieved literature for any of the twelve factors, so its role in this account is inferential, not evidenced.
